summary: chain.from_iterable yields every item of the first iterable, then every item of the next, and so on.
documentation: chain.from_iterable yields every item of the first iterable, then every item of the next, and so on. It traverses one level lazily without building intermediate concatenations. Converting the iterator to a list creates a JSON-compatible result.
inputs: A list of lists containing JSON values.
returns: One flattened list in original order.
caution: This flattens only one level. A nested list encountered as an item remains a list; strings would be iterated character by character if supplied as inner iterables.
scenarios: Combine pages of locally loaded search results.
Flatten daily groups of checklist items into one work queue.
Join batches of imported identifiers while keeping order.
title: Flatten batches once
problem: Input is a list of lists. Flatten exactly one level, preserving values, duplicates, order and any deeper nested lists.
goal: Use itertools.chain.from_iterable() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Import chain and wrap chain.from_iterable(value) with list.
